statement: h01's money-critical manifest is implemented as an in-source attribute (#[money_critical(registered)] / #[money_critical(exempt)]) at the point of definition, NOT a separate out-of-band manifest file, even though the workpack text says 'appear in the money-critical manifest (the serde record)'. There is no dedicated manifest-record type; the attribute IS the registration, colocated with the code it describes.
why: An external path-keyed manifest file can silently drift from a moved/renamed function (the exact 'silence != permission' failure mode the doctrine warns about); a colocated attribute cannot drift without the diff being visible in the same review as the code change. h02/h03/h05/h06 (which consume this manifest read-only per the workpack) should read the #[money_critical(..)] attribute + the MONEY-CRIT-CLASSIFY.1 scoring signal, not a separate JSON/serde file that does not exist.
howToApply: Any h02/h03/h05/h06 lane building on h01: do not expect a money-critical.json manifest file with per-unit entries. Re-run (or import) crates/enforcer-security/src/rules/money_critical.rs's score_unit + is_registered/is_exempt helpers, or scan for the #[money_critical(registered)] attribute textually, to determine which units are in-manifest. Do not redefine the classification signal families — only MONEY-CRIT-CLASSIFY.1 owns that scoring.

statement: enforcer-security had no syn/proc-macro2 dependency yet (unlike enforcer-lang-rust). Adding syn = { version = "2", features = ["full","extra-traits","visit"] } alone compiles but Spanned::span().start() fails at runtime-compile with 'no method named start found for struct proc_macro2::Span' unless proc-macro2 is ALSO added directly with the span-locations feature (syn re-exports proc_macro2::Span but does not itself forward that cargo feature transitively for callers).
why: First cargo check pass on the new money_critical.rs module failed with E0599 on spanned.span().start().line despite enforcer-lang-rust's near-identical no_reexports.rs using the exact same call successfully — the difference was enforcer-lang-rust's Cargo.toml has an explicit proc-macro2 = { version = "1", features = ["span-locations"] } line that enforcer-security lacked.
howToApply: When adding syn-based AST validators to a NEW crate (not enforcer-lang-rust, which already has this wired), always add BOTH syn (with needed features) AND proc-macro2 = { version = "1", features = ["span-locations"] } to that crate's [dependencies] — grep an existing lang-* crate's Cargo.toml for the exact proc-macro2 line rather than assuming syn's transitive feature forwarding covers it.

statement: enforcer-security's rules/registry.rs and tests/completeness.rs are the shared Validator-registration seam every Track H feature pack (d18, h01-h08, h11) extends, per the crate's own doc comments. registry.rs's pre-existing unit test 'registry_builds_cleanly' hard-coded assert_eq!(rows.len(), 1) — adding new rows to build_all() without updating that assertion breaks the arc-19 skeleton owner's own test, even though registry.rs itself is explicitly the seam every pack is TOLD to extend.
why: The workpack's 'lib.rs/mod.rs additions: ONLY your lines' instruction could be read as 'never touch a line someone else wrote', but registry.rs's own module doc says 'Feature packs add their own rows here as they land their src/rules/<name>.rs' — the count-assertion in its test is not itself owned content, it is a byproduct that MUST be widened (not touched destructively) whenever a new row lands, or the crate fails its own pre-existing test suite.
howToApply: When extending enforcer-security's registry.rs build_all() seam, always check rules/registry.rs's own #[cfg(test)] block for a hard-coded rows.len() assertion and widen it (assert on your new rule_id's presence via an .any() check, keep the total count accurate) rather than leaving it stale — completeness.rs (a SEPARATE file, genuinely not in h01's owns) is deliberately loose and does NOT need touching (it only asserts no-duplicates + H00-1.1 presence).

statement: enforcer_mechanization::parity::ParityOracle::check_doc_anchor treats a doc-anchor '#fragment' as a LITERAL SUBSTRING match against the target file's raw text (contents.contains(fragment)), not a Markdown heading-slug resolution. A docAnchor like '...md#requirement-checklist' against a heading literally written '## Requirement Checklist' FAILS parity, because the slug text never appears verbatim in the file.
why: Discovered by writing a whole-registry parity test (tests/money_critical_parity.rs) against a freshly-authored rules/money-critical.json: the first docAnchor draft used a slugified fragment guess and the oracle sweep correctly flagged it as a parity gap, forcing a switch to a fragment string that is guaranteed to appear verbatim in the target doc (here, the literal rule-id token 'MONEY-CRIT-CLASSIFY' that already appears in the workpack's checklist bullet text).
howToApply: When authoring any new RuleRecord.docAnchor with a '#fragment', pick a fragment that is a literal substring already present in the target doc's raw text (e.g. a rule-id token, an exact heading string with correct case/no dashes) — do not assume CommonMark heading-slug conversion; verify with grep -n '<fragment>' <doc-file> before trusting the parity oracle to pass.
